scope: Audit whether the random-photo repeated world-map design sufficiently fixes the analysis target before downstream inference. This is a methodological audit, not a new biological test.

overall_assessment.adequate_for: Inference conditional on the frozen iNaturalist-derived candidate availability surface, the location-blind measurement system, the postmeasurement classifiability gate, and the frozen repeated-atlas schedule.
overall_assessment.not_equivalent_to: An unbiased census of all angiosperm individuals, species, regions, or photographs on Earth.

audit.evidence: A frozen metadata-first candidate programme defined the photo/species universe before colour pixels were opened, and the later measurement budget selected 500 species and 100 candidate photographs per species without colour outcomes.
audit.remaining_limit: The candidate universe inherits platform participation, observer geography, taxon availability, flowering annotation, licence, coordinate-quality, and image-availability filters.

audit.evidence: 50,000 measurement rows reached terminal colour-measurement states before coordinates were joined to colour outputs; 25,377 were classifiable and 24,623 mixed/uncertain.
audit.remaining_limit: Classifiability is substantial structural missingness and may vary geographically or taxonomically even though location was not used to measure colour.

audit.evidence: The >=40 classifiable-photo rule yielded 369 eligible species before G1/G3 inference and was not altered after seeing the primary result.
audit.remaining_limit: The estimand is the eligible measured-species population, not all originally sampled species.

audit.evidence: 200 outer realizations x 250 species x 20 photographs were frozen with fixed species/photo seeds; every eligible species appears 135-136 times and long-run species/photo inclusion imbalance is at most one.
audit.remaining_limit: Monte Carlo field convergence at 100 versus 200 realizations fell just below the predeclared strong-stability correlation threshold, so convergence strength still needs diagnostic quantification.

audit.evidence: Species total geometric weight is equalized within each outer realization and field intensity is divided by the same geographic opportunity support used in the numerator.
audit.remaining_limit: This controls the declared opportunity field but does not create observations in geographic/taxonomic regions poorly represented by the platform.

audit.evidence: A pre-colour platform-effort audit found very high cell-level concordance between target-group and all-platform record intensity, indicating that generic platform activity is a major component of availability.
audit.remaining_limit: The audit characterizes but does not fully remove platform or target-group availability bias.

audit.evidence: No species/photo replacement after measurement, fixed null indices/seeds, separate authorizations, and explicit no-rescue rules are recorded throughout the analysis lineage.
audit.remaining_limit: None requiring redesign of the current upstream sampling target.

quantitative_followups_required: Estimate G1 detectability and type-I behaviour under the actual clustered photo geometry.

Compare detectability using the actual classifiable 369-species pool versus the full 500-species measured-coordinate pool with synthetic outcomes, to quantify the cost of classifiability attrition without reopening biological outcomes.
Quantify how consensus-field stability changes with the number of outer realizations using simulation/bootstrap rather than extending the frozen observed primary schedule to chase the stability gate.
Quantify power to detect partial rather than universal recurrence when only a fraction of species share a latent transition architecture.
interpretation_boundary: The repeated random-photo atlas is methodologically mature enough to continue downstream. Its main unresolved upstream issue is not target-definition ambiguity but how platform geometry, missingness, partial sharing, and finite repeated sampling affect detectability and stability.
